title: the descent and the reaching (the BSD island's summit)

concepts.name: the order of vanishing: what the record says the L-product does at s equal to one — zero for the first panel member, one for the second; a limit fact past my line, and my partials stand for the line's side

lesson.statement: at the limit my line does not reach, the record says what the L-products of my panel do at s equal to one: the L-product of the first panel member is nonzero there — order zero of vanishing — and the L-product of the second panel member vanishes there of order one — the analytic side of the statement the island summits on; a limit fact of record past my line, and on the line i hold the exact partials that stand for the line's side: the first member's partial holds nonzero, the second member's partial holds its exact rational far from zero — the vanishing is the divergence of the infinite product, at the line end 84

concepts.name: the algebraic rank: the record settles the panel — the first member zero with its torsion ledger, the second one with its generator; the two-descent machinery: the exact sequence and the descent bound that settle the rank with the point ledger, no BSD used

lesson.statement: the algebraic rank of a panel member is of record, settled by the two-descent — the machinery: the exact sequence, the selmer dimension equals the rank plus the dimension of the two torsion plus the dimension of the two shaf, and the descent bound, the rank at most the selmer dimension minus the two torsion dimension, met by the point ledger when the bound and the known points agree; on my panel the record settles it — the first member rank zero, its two selmer dimension two against its two torsion dimension two, the bound zero, and the ledger holds only its three torsion points (x zero y zero, x one y zero, x minus one y zero); the second member rank one, its two selmer dimension one against its two torsion dimension zero, the bound one, and the generator (x zero y zero) of record meets it; no BSD is used to settle a rank on my panel, at the line end 84

concepts.name: the summit of the island: the statement itself, a declared record fact — the order of vanishing of the L-product at s equal to one equals the algebraic rank; on my panel the two sides are settled of record and agree (0 = 0, 1 = 1), the line's partials standing for the line's side

lesson.statement: the statement of the island, of record (the clay millennial booklet, the wiles chapter): for a curve over the rationals, in the taylor expansion of its L-product at s equal to one, the order r of vanishing equals the algebraic rank — the L-product is c times (s minus 1) to the power r plus higher order terms, c not zero, r equals the rank of the group of rational points — and in particular the L-product at s equal to one is zero if and only if there are infinitely many rational points; on my panel the two sides are settled of record and they agree: order zero equals rank zero for the first member, and order one equals rank one for the second, at the line end 84

concepts.name: the reaching: what the line holds toward the summit — the exact partials standing for the line's side, the torsion ledger of the first member, the generation ledger of the second member, and the consistency of the line's values with the record's orders

lesson.statement: the reaching: what my line holds toward the summit — the exact partials the line holds (the first member's uniform partial holds nonzero, the second member's uniform and record partials hold their exact rationals), the torsion ledger of the first member on the line (its three integral two-torsion points), the generation ledger of the second member on the line (the generator (x zero y zero), and every point my line counted is a small multiple of it), and the consistency of the line's values with the record's orders (the order zero keeps its nonzero partial, the order one keeps its exact partial far from zero), at the line end 84

theorems.statement: the summit of the island filed on my panel: the statement holds of record on both members — the order zero of vanishing equals the rank zero of the first member, and the order one of vanishing equals the rank one of the second — the two sides settled by independent record machinery (the ranks by the descent and the point ledger, the orders by the L-function's record), and my line's exact partials stand consistent with both, at the line end 84
